items: Audit Your Burnout Source: Create three separate columns labeling them project stress, role dysfunction, and industry-wide problems to diagnose where most of your suffering actually originates.
Audit Your Burnout Source: Spend 30 minutes writing down specific examples of what you hate, placing each item in the appropriate column rather than keeping it vague and unexamined.
Audit Your Burnout Source: Put checkmarks next to the five items in each column that feel most true on your worst days to identify your real non-negotiable pain points.
Audit Your Burnout Source: Determine whether most of your pain lives in the industry column, which signals that no role within creative work will solve your burnout.
Identify Hidden Transferable Skills: Break free from defining yourself as just a video editor by listing every tool, process, and workflow you use routinely in your current work.
Identify Hidden Transferable Skills: Write out what you actually do all day beyond operating software, including how you translate vague direction into concrete technical results.

Identify Hidden Transferable Skills: Identify instances where you manage competing priorities across multiple projects simultaneously, which represents a high-value skill businesses outside creative industries desperately need.
Identify Hidden Transferable Skills: Recognize that your daily practice of making fast decisions under pressure is a sophisticated professional competency that applies far beyond the edit suite.
Prepare Your Exit Strategy: Build a financial buffer before making any career changes so that desperation does not force you into another exploitative role out of immediate necessity.
Prepare Your Exit Strategy: Research alternative roles and industries that your transferable skills could serve, focusing on sectors you have not previously considered as possibilities.
Prepare Your Exit Strategy: Develop a transition plan that leverages your existing technical expertise instead of requiring you to start from zero in an entirely unfamiliar field.
Prepare Your Exit Strategy: Create a timeline for your exit that protects your finances and professional identity while giving you space to make deliberate choices rather than panicked ones.
